reports.title: AMG Reports Financial and Operating Results for the Third Quarter and Nine Months Ended 2026

desk.headline: Economic EPS up 56% to $9.50, beat; revenue $595m below estimates; record $974bn AUM; Q4 outlook given on call
results: Net client inflows of $20.7bn, led by record alternatives inflows of over $31bn (liquid alternatives $21.9bn, private markets $9.6bn); long-only equities lost $11.9bn.
Assets under management hit a record $973.9bn, up from $942.4bn at end-June.
Adjusted EBITDA rose 41% to $354m and economic EPS 56% to $9.50; GAAP EPS dipped to $6.64 because last year included a $127.6m gain on the Peppertree sale.
Bought back $400m of shares in the quarter ($775m so far this year); quarterly dividend $0.01.

guidance.summary: The press release has no outlook. On the call management guided Q4 adjusted EBITDA of $405–475m and economic EPS of $11.37–13.43, and said 2026 economic EPS should grow about 50%.

points: Alternatives now produce roughly two-thirds or more of EBITDA, versus under a third in 2019.
Buybacks are planned at over $900m this year, with management saying there is plenty of room to keep repurchasing.
The deal pipeline is described as strong after adding BBH Credit Partners and HighBrook Investors.
Analysts pressed on reliance on tax-aware long/short strategies amid custodian limits and tax-rule developments; management acknowledged uncertainty.
The Q4 outlook assumes markets about 2% lower quarter-to-date and no material catch-up fees.
